nodes.name: Printing Letter_Invoices
nodes.notes: Returns one item per account, carrying the letter content and the customer number. Does NOT carry the email address — that is looked up from Business Central further down.

nodes.name: Normalize Account Fields
nodes.notes: Fallback chains cover both Business Central shapes: OData page fields (No, Name, Company_Name, Integration_Customer_No) and API v2.0 fields (number, displayName, companyName). Trim to the single real field name once the Printing Letter_Invoices export is available. accountNumber must end up as the customer number (e.g. 10981) — it is the key for the contact lookup.

nodes.name: Require Account Number
nodes.notes: Guard: an empty account number would turn the BC $filter into a match-everything query and would render the wrong account's statement.

nodes.name: Look Up AP Contact (Business Central)
nodes.notes: Queries the Contact List page (5052 / table 5050) published as the OData web service 'ContactList', filtered to the contact whose Integration Customer No. matches this customer — the CT020141 -> 10981 link. Reads BC_TENANT_ID, BC_ENVIRONMENT and BC_COMPANY_NAME from project Variables. If the published web service has a different name, change the last URL segment.

nodes.name: Printing Statements
nodes.notes: Runs once per account, keyed on accountNumber, so the statement pulled from Business Central is the one for this customer and lines up with this letter. Returns exactly one item carrying the statement PDF as binary data. NOTE: the accountNumber input mapping above only applies if this workflow's Execute Workflow Trigger declares a matching input field. If that trigger is set to 'Accept all data' instead, delete the mapping — accountNumber already rides along on the item. Lives in My project / Engelman's Bakery / Printing Letter_Invoices.

nodes.name: Combine Letter + Statement
nodes.notes: Input 1 = letter/account/email data, Input 2 = statement PDF. Position pairing is safe because Printing Statements runs once per item, in order. Clash handling prefers input 1 so a field the statement workflow happens to return (its own accountNumber or No) cannot overwrite the account identity the draft is addressed from.

nodes.name: Create Outlook Draft (Do Not Send)
nodes.notes: Creates an UNSENT draft only. The draft lands in the mailbox that owns the OAuth2 credential, so this credential must be gpress@engelmansbakery.com. There is deliberately no 'send' operation anywhere in this workflow.

nodes.name: Skipped — No Email on File
nodes.notes: Accounts whose Business Central contact has no usable E-Mail land here instead of silently disappearing. Review this branch after each run — contactMatchCount of 0 means no contact matched the customer number at all.
